First, the total time Eric spends on his trip to the park is 20 minutes running + 10 minutes jogging = 30 minutes.
The trip back home takes 3 times longer than his original trip, so the total time to return home is 3 times 30 minutes = 90 minutes.
However, since Eric starts his return trip when he is halfway through his running and jogging, we need to subtract half of his running time and half of his jogging time from the total time.
Half of his running time is 20 minutes / 2 = 10 minutes.
Half of his jogging time is 10 minutes / 2 = 5 minutes.
So, Eric needs to subtract 10 minutes + 5 minutes from the total time, resulting in 90 minutes - 15 minutes = 75 minutes.
Therefore, it takes Eric 75 minutes to return home.
